title: Why Robert Pattinson Could Be a Great James Bond
summary: Robert Pattinson’s gift for portraying petulant losers would seem at odds with the requirements for 007. But the actor may be just what the franchise needs.

By


[Alissa Wilkinson](https://www.nytimes.com/by/alissa-wilkinson)


Nov. 16, 2026


Robert Pattinson excels at playing a weird little guy, a pathetic loser, a man in need of a vacation. His breakthrough was as a tortured vampire, after all. He’s rarely a well-adjusted square, let alone a smooth, cosmopolitan type like James Bond, the role he won on Monday.


And he seems to love those misfits. When I[spoke with him in 2019](https://www.vox.com/culture/2019/10/16/20914108/robert-pattinson-interview-lighthouse) , just before Robert Eggers’s “The Lighthouse” was released, he was enthusiastic about the challenge that came with parts that “go so hard”: “The danger is you kind of just want to make every part crazy and just ratchet the intensity up as high as possible.”


No kidding. The joy of seeing Pattinson’s credit on a movie is knowing you’re in for a wild ride; he’ll never do what you expect. He’s worked with a long, enviable list of auteurs, each with a distinctive style into which Pattinson has somehow managed to fit. He brings an off-kilter quality and — despite his charisma and success — a real gift for petulant losers.


In Josh and Benny Safdie’s 2017 grimy nightmare, “[Good Time](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/10/movies/good-time-review-robert-pattinson.html) ,” he’s a small-time criminal who’s having a very bad night. In 2024, he played several versions of the same character in Bong Joon Ho’s “Mickey 17,” one of whom is an anxious, submissive drone. Last year, he starred opposite Jennifer Lawrence in Lynne Ramsay’s “[Die My Love](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/06/movies/die-my-love-review.html) ,” and took the clueless husband role to wretchedly sulky new heights. His lighthouse keeper in “[The Lighthouse](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/10/16/movies/the-lighthouse-review.html) ” was literally insane by the end, crawling on the floor, psychologically obliterated.


Image


Robert Pattinson took the clueless husband to sulky heights in “Die My Love,” starring Jennifer Lawrence.


Credit...


Kimberly French/Mubi


“I hope to keep finding stuff like that again,” he told me. “I want everything to be as crazy as this.”
